ShortDescription.Value: Fixes the tourism simulation: tourists arrive by plane and ferry, spend money in your shops, hotels and motels get their own zones, and the numbers finally mean something.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Tourism Overhaul
Cities: Skylines II ships tourism with several defects that make the whole feature feel inert. You can max out city attractiveness and still see almost no visitors. This mod fixes the causes.
Every change was derived by decompiling and tracing the game's own assemblies, not by guesswork. The full trace, with the file and line behind each finding, is on the GitHub page.
## Tourists actually arrive
The base game picks each tourist's transport mode with one random roll — 10% road, 10% train, 50% air, 30% sea — then looks for an outside connection of exactly that type. If your city doesn't have one, it gives up. No fallback, no retry. But the tourist household is still created, just without a location, and a household with no location can never be given any people. It's silently deleted moments later.
On a city with no airport and no harbour, that destroys 80% of all tourist arrivals.
This mod redistributes the share across the connection types your city actually has, and keeps the intended preference for planes and ferries once you build an airport or harbour.
## Arrivals route around congestion
The base game has no capacity concept for outside connections at all. A saturated airport keeps receiving its full share, and any tourist who can't travel onward from it is deleted rather than rerouted.
This mod watches how many tourists are still waiting at each entrance and shifts arrivals toward routes that are moving. Build a harbour and it starts carrying real traffic.
## Tourism scales with your city
The base game targets attractiveness x 15 tourists, and attractiveness itself is capped at 100 — a flat 1,500 visitors whether you're a town or a metropolis. Past that ceiling, every extra park and landmark does nothing at all.
This mod scales the target with population, so a large attractive city supports a proportionate number of visitors. Fully tunable, with a safety ceiling.
## Tourists have a real length of stay
The game declares a tourist departure timer, saves it, and never reads it. It also has a function returning a random stay length that nothing ever calls. Both are unfinished.
This mod implements the mechanic using the field the game already has, so visits have a believable duration and turnover instead of guests lingering until their money runs out.
## Hotels and motels get their own zones
The game already ships proper hotel and motel buildings — 80 of them, in both European and North American styles, at every level and lot size. You just can't ask for one. They sit mixed in with ordinary shops in the commercial zones, so zoning commercial gives you a hotel maybe one lot in four, wherever the game feels like putting it.
This mod adds two new zones to the zoning toolbar, Hotels and Motels, and moves those buildings into them. Hotels stop turning up in ordinary commercial zones, so your tourist district goes where you want it — by the beach, near the airport, around the old town — instead of scattered across the map.
Both come with their own icons, drawn to match the game's existing zone art.
A note on removal: zone painting is stored as a plain number in your save, so hotel zoning won't mean anything if you later uninstall the mod. That's true of any mod that adds a zone. Everything else here is safe to add and remove freely.
## The numbers finally mean something
The tourism panel computes a figure around eight times larger than the simulation can ever produce, and its tourist count ignores everyone travelling between destinations.
This mod reports the real values and adds three rows to the Tourism info view:
- Tourists in city — current against the number your city can sustain - Hotel rooms free — free against total, across every hotel - Local cims away — your own residents currently on holiday elsewhere
## Tourists spend money in your city
In the base game a visitor never once sets foot in a shop. Citizens choose shopping over sightseeing whenever their household wants something, but that want comes from supplies running low at home — and a visitor has no home and no cupboard, so it never happens. They sightsee for their entire stay, and the only money that reaches your economy is the hotel bill.
This mod gives visitors a reason to shop. Your commercial districts start earning from tourism, and the crowds in the park thin out because there is somewhere else worth going.
How keenly they shop is adjustable, and can be turned off entirely.
## Historic districts draw visitors
Attractiveness in the base game comes almost entirely from parks and signature landmarks. An ordinary building contributes nothing, however beautiful, so a preserved old quarter draws nobody unless a landmark happens to sit inside it.
Mark a building as historical and it now adds to your city's appeal. One old house counts for very little; a whole preserved street or quarter is worth travelling for. Tourism becomes something a district can earn through its character, instead of something you place.
## Visitors can afford their stay
Leisure is where a visitor's money actually goes, and in the base game it goes fast. Visitors have no cooldown between outings, so they go out constantly, and at the game's own prices a visitor can run themselves broke in well under a day and leave long before their stay is up. Tourist numbers then collapse in waves for no visible reason.
This mod lowers what a visit to a museum, park or bar costs, so a visitor's spending money lasts the length of stay they were given and the turnover you see is people going home rather than people going bankrupt. Your own citizens get cheaper days out too — the price belongs to the venue, not the customer — and the venues earn less per visit in exchange.
Adjustable, and returnable to the base game's pricing if you prefer it.
## Optional extras
- Hotel room multiplier, 1x to 10x, for zoned commercial hotels. Signature buildings keep their authored capacity. The city's sense of how many rooms it needs scales with this, so raising it makes hotels bigger without making the city think it has enough of them. - Residents take holidays. The base game suppresses out-of-town travel to roughly 1-3% of leisure trips and blocks it entirely for households with no spare money. Turn this up and your citizens will use your airport too. - A coloured ring marker under tourists so you can pick them out of a crowd, with adjustable colour and size.
Everything is individually toggleable, and everything is off or at vanilla values by default except the arrival fixes.
## Tourism has a demand bar
The base game shows you demand for residential, commercial, industrial and office, and nothing for tourism — so there is no way to tell whether your city could support more visitors, or what is stopping it.
This mod adds a seventh demand bar, in light red. It sits with the others in the City Information panel and in the toolbar, and it reads as visitors who would come but have nowhere to stay — so it is highest when your city is appealing and every room is taken, and falls to nothing once there is a room waiting for everyone who wants one.
Underneath it, the same kind of factor list the other six have, saying what is actually holding tourism back — not enough hotel rooms, rooms standing empty, attractiveness, visitors already here, or the ways into your city. Hover it and the panel explains it, exactly as it does for the rest.
The bar is drawn by the game rather than by the mod, so it matches the others precisely.
## In your language
The zones, the info views, the panel rows and every setting are translated into all eleven other languages the game ships with: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.
The long explanatory text under each setting stays in English. Those descriptions run to several paragraphs of simulation detail, and a confidently wrong translation is worse than an English one because you cannot tell that it is wrong. Corrections and additions from native speakers are very welcome on GitHub.
## Compatibility
No Harmony patches and no reflection. Arrivals use real outside connections, real vehicles, real pathfinding, real hotels and the real economy. Safe to add to an existing save, and safe to remove.
The optional hotel room multiplier replaces the game's lodging system with a copy that applies the multiplier — this is unavoidable, because room count is computed inside a compiled job from values that also control rent and workplaces. Turning the setting off restores the original system immediately. Leave it off if you'd rather nothing native is replaced.
Source, full technical writeup and issue tracker: https://github.com/Meapy/CS2-TourismOverhaul
Publish.ChangeLog:
1.8.0
Cruise ships.
There is a new Passenger Cruise Line tool beside the passenger ship line. Draw it from a sea outside connection to a harbour and a cruise ship works the route: it fills with visitors at the map edge, sails in, ties up at your quay while its passengers spend the day in your city, and leaves with them at the end of shore leave. Cruise passengers sleep aboard, so they never take a hotel room and never compete with your other visitors for one — they go shopping, to your attractions and to your leisure venues instead.
Nobody is teleported or placed by hand at any point. The mod creates visitors at the connection and gives them a reason to travel; the game gives them bodies, routes them, boards them and lands them through its own machinery. Passengers walk off the pier, wander the city, and run back to the quay when last call goes out.
Select a docked cruise ship and the panel tells you when it sails and how many of its passengers are still out in the city, so you can see a call running down rather than guessing at it.
Two settings: cruise shore leave in hours, defaulting to 8, and how many passengers a call brings. The ship's own capacity applies as well, and the smaller of the two wins.
One cruise line per city, from a sea outside connection to a single harbour. The tool disappears once a line exists and returns if you delete it. Everything the feature does is written to the harbour and the map-edge stop rather than to the line, so two of them would overwrite each other.
Known limitation: a harbour shared between a cruise line and an ordinary passenger ship line is affected by both. Give the cruise line its own terminal if you can. Removing the mod while a ship is alongside leaves a lodging marker on the harbour — do it between voyages.
Saves from earlier versions load unchanged.
